title: Find Minimum In Rotated Sorted Array
statement: A sorted array of distinct integers was rotated: some items from the end were moved to the front, keeping their order. You get the rotated array. Return its smallest value in O(log n) time.

example.caption: 0 1 2 4 5 6 7 was rotated so that 4 5 6 7 come first. The smallest value 0 now sits where the order drops.

idea.sentence: Compare the middle with the right end. If the middle is bigger, the drop is to its right. If not, the right side is in order and the minimum is the middle or left of it.

jargon.plain: Cut a sorted array at one spot and swap the two pieces. You get a high run followed by a low run, with one drop between them.
A fact that stays true on every loop turn. Here: the minimum is always inside nums[l..r].

watch.inputHint: One argument: a rotated sorted array of distinct numbers, e.g. [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]

rows.name: Linear scan
rows.note: Works on any array, and ignores the structure.

rows.name: Binary search
rows.note: Each middle check removes half of the candidates. Only l, m and r are kept.

fast.takeaway: The array is not sorted, but it is sorted in two runs. One comparison with the right end says which run the middle is in.

stages.title: Candidates
stages.note: l and r bound the part of the array that must still hold the minimum.

stages.title: Middle vs right end
stages.note: While two or more cells remain, take the middle m and compare nums[m] with nums[r].

stages.title: Middle is in the high run
stages.note: nums[m] > nums[r] means the drop is to the right of m, so l = m + 1.

stages.title: Middle is in the low run
stages.note: Otherwise nums[m] could be the minimum itself, so keep it: r = m.

stages.title: One cell left
stages.note: l equals r. That cell is the minimum.

edges.title: Not rotated
edges.why: The middle is never bigger than the right end, so r keeps pulling in until it reaches index 0.

edges.title: Single element
edges.why: l = r from the start, so the loop is skipped and nums[0] is returned.

edges.title: Two elements, swapped
edges.why: m = 0, and 2 > 1, so l = 1. Rounding the middle down keeps nums[m] from being compared with itself.

edges.title: Minimum is last
edges.why: The middle 4 is bigger than 1 every time, so l keeps moving right until it lands on the last cell.

gotchas.text: (l + r) / 2 can be 2.5. Use l + Math.floor((r - l) / 2), otherwise nums[m] is undefined and every comparison with it is false.
m = l + (r-l)/2 rounds down, which is what keeps r = m from looping forever. Rounding up would make m = r and r = m would never shrink the range.
Compare with nums[r], not nums[l]. If the middle is at l (two cells left), nums[m] > nums[l] is false and gives a misleading answer for [2, 1].
Here the loop is l < r and r = m, not l <= r and r = m - 1. We are narrowing to one cell, not looking for an exact match. Mixing the two styles can loop forever.

recap.pattern: Binary search on a rotated array
recap.key: The minimum sits at the drop. If nums[m] is bigger than nums[r], the drop is right of m. Otherwise it is at m or left of it.
moves: While l < r, take m = l + (r - l) / 2
nums[m] > nums[r]: l = m + 1. Otherwise r = m
